samples.name: x01-fake-mcp-server
samples.technique: Fake MCP server: on start it reads AI-tool configs and cloud keys, sends them over HTTPS, and registers itself in Claude Desktop so it starts with the AI app.
samples.source: FakeGit (Island, Jul 2026: 800+ repos posing as MCP servers / AI skills); rogue-MCP typosquats on npm (2026)

samples.name: x02-poisoned-poc
samples.technique: Poisoned proof-of-concept exploit: a lone exploit.py whose 'dependency check' decodes and runs a collector that sends SSH/AWS keys, shell history and the Hugging Face token to a raw IP.
samples.source: El Yadmani et al., 'Beyond the Surface' (Leiden; 1.9-10.3% of 47k GitHub PoC repos malicious); fake LDAPNightmare PoC with an infostealer (Trend Micro, Jan 2025)

samples.name: x03-fake-ai-tool
samples.technique: Fake 'local LLM studio' AI tool: at start it 'checks cached models', reads the Hugging Face token, MCP configs, another project's .env and a Solana wallet, and sends them to a Hugging Face lookalike host.
samples.source: GitVenom (Kaspersky, Feb 2025: AI-written READMEs, fake AI/automation tools); Water Curse / Banana Squad (2025)

samples.name: x04-deadbugz-mcp
samples.technique: MCP server that is clean until the 3rd tool call, then steals SSH and AI-tool keys; its tool description also hides instructions for the AI (tool poisoning).
samples.source: Deadbugz (Pillar Security, Aug 2026: activates after 3 tool calls); Invariant Labs tool-poisoning research (2025)

samples.name: x05-pickle-model
samples.technique: Model whose pytorch_model.bin pickle runs code when loaded (torch.load with weights_only=False, older PyTorch): sends the Hugging Face token, AWS keys, SSH key and Claude config to a raw IP.
samples.source: JFrog (2024: ~100 malicious models, ~95% PyTorch pickles); nullifAI (ReversingLabs, Feb 2025)

samples.name: x06-remote-code-model
samples.technique: Model with custom code (auto_map -> modeling_fast.py): loading it with trust_remote_code=True runs the model class, which sends the Hugging Face token, MCP keys and a wallet to a lookalike CDN.
samples.source: trust_remote_code bypasses in Transformers / Diffusers (CVE-2026-4372, FaceHugger, 2026)

samples.name: x07-sleeper-extension
samples.technique: Sleeper VS Code extension: after activation it reads the SSH key, MetaMask vault, git and Claude configs, uploads them, then copies itself into Cursor, Windsurf and VS Code extension folders.
samples.source: GlassWorm on Open VSX (Socket, Mar-Apr 2026: 70+ sleeper extensions, installs itself into every IDE it finds)

samples.name: y01-clean-mcp-server
samples.technique: Clean MCP server: answers tools/list on stdio, reads only its own project file, no network.

samples.name: y02-clean-poc
samples.technique: Clean proof-of-concept: one script that sends the crafted request to the target and reports.

samples.name: y03-clean-hf-script
samples.technique: Clean ML script: reads its Hugging Face token like huggingface_hub does and sends it to huggingface.co (the false-alarm case for the new AI bait).

samples.name: y04-clean-s3-mcp
samples.technique: Clean MCP server that does read ~/.aws/credentials on a tool call and calls S3 with it (the false-alarm case for tool-calling: a credential used with its own service).

samples.name: y05-clean-pickle-model
samples.technique: Clean model: an ordinary PyTorch-format checkpoint (tensors only) with a config.json.

samples.name: y07-clean-extension
samples.technique: Clean VS Code extension: registers a command, reads its settings, writes its own storage folder.
